SELF-HOST ON macOS APPLE SILICON (Python 3.14-safe — no pip/torch):
1. Download the prebuilt engine from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech-Engine/releases (macOS arm64 asset) OR reuse the copy bundled inside the desktop app at /Applications/AivisSpeech.app/Contents/Resources/AivisSpeech-Engine/run . It ships its own ONNX Runtime — CPU-only is fine, no GPU, needs macOS 13+ and ~1.5GB RAM. This avoids the Python 3.14 / torch wheel problem entirely (the engine does NOT use your system Python).
2. Run it: it listens on http://127.0.0.1:10101 by default. Interactive API docs at http://127.0.0.1:10101/docs .
3. Install voice models: download each .aivmx from AivisHub (button on each model's hub.aivis-project.com/aivm-models/<uuid> page, or POST to the engine's aivm install endpoint) and drop into ~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models — the engine auto-discovers on start. GET /speakers lists loaded voices + their per-style speaker UUIDs.

STORY SYNTHESIS (VOICEVOX-compatible, per line):
4. POST /audio_query?text=<line>&speaker=<styleId>  → returns an AudioQuery JSON.
5. Optionally tweak AudioQuery.speedScale / pitchScale / intonationScale (global, these DO work) for the rainy-evening calm delivery, and pick the emotion style per line by choosing the right speaker style id (rasetsun exposes 標準/標準2/悲しみ/etc.).
6. POST /synthesis?speaker=<styleId> with the AudioQuery body → WAV. Cache 323 WAVs keyed by (line, speaker, style).

PITCH-ACCENT DRILL LANE (learner-safe):
7. The AudioQuery.accent_phrases array carries mora units and an integer `accent` = nucleus position per phrase; the engine honors that placement, so you can force heiban/atamadaka/nakadaka/odaka by editing `accent` before /synthesis. This is the correct knob for drill/imitation audio.
8. HARD LIMIT to record: the per-mora numeric `pitch` (and consonant_length/vowel_length) fields are dummy 0.0 and NOT editable in the AivisSpeech Engine — so you can move the accent nucleus but cannot hand-tune a pitch contour. If the drill spec needs exact per-mora Hz shaping, that requires raw Style-Bert-VITS2-JP-Extra in Python (blocked here by Python 3.14 → would need a 3.11 venv/conda or a container). Recommend accepting accent-position control as the offline drill path and flagging the pitch-contour limitation to the owner.

LICENSE HYGIENE AT SHIP: ACML-1.0 credit is optional but keep an in-app attribution/credits list anyway; add an "unofficial / not affiliated with the voice provider" line in credits to stay clear of the impersonation clause; if you redistribute any .aivmx, bundle the full ACML-1.0 text alongside it (redistribution requires including the license).

recipes.lane: HuggingFace + AivisHub Style-Bert-VITS2 JP-Extra models with commercial-clean licenses; self-hosted offline TTS via the AivisSpeech Engine on macOS Apple Silicon.
recipes.recipe:
=== ENGINE / OFFLINE SELF-HOST (macOS Apple Silicon, Python 3.14 present) ===
Do NOT pip-install Style-Bert-VITS2 (needs torch<2.4 which has no wheels for Python 3.14, and the SBV2 code is AGPL-3.0). Use the AivisSpeech Engine — it ships its own bundled runtime, no system Python.

1. Install: download AivisSpeech.app (or the standalone AivisSpeech-Engine release) from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech-Engine/releases. Bundled engine binary lives at /Applications/AivisSpeech.app/Contents/Resources/AivisSpeech-Engine/run.
2. First run downloads default models (~250MB) + BERT (~650MB). IMPORTANT: the factory default voice is Anneli — swap it out (see reject) so it never ends up in shipped audio.
3. Run headless API: `.../AivisSpeech-Engine/run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 10101` (VOICEVOX-compatible HTTP server, default port 10101; --host 0.0.0.0 to expose).
4. Install voices: drop AIVMX files in `~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models`, or POST via the engine's model-management API, or AivisSpeech UI → Settings → Manage voice synthesis models (one-click install straight from AivisHub).

=== SYNTHESIS + LEARNER-SAFE ACCENT DRILL ===
5. POST /audio_query?speaker=<style_id>&text=<JA> → returns AudioQuery with accent_phrases[] → moras[] (text/consonant/vowel/pitch) and an accent index (downstep position) per phrase.
6. For DRILL audio: read/patch accent_phrases[].accent to set the correct pitch-accent nucleus — SBV2 JP-Extra renders that high/low mora pattern faithfully, so drills stay accent-correct. NOTE: consonant_length/vowel_length/pitch scalar fields return DUMMY values and are ignored by this engine — do not rely on them for fine F0; the accent-nucleus field is the lever.
7. POST /synthesis?speaker=<style_id> with the (patched) AudioQuery JSON → WAV. Each speaker style is a separate speaker/style id in /speakers.

=== GETTING NON-AIVMX MODELS (JVNV, RikkaBotan) INTO THE ENGINE ===
8. JVNV and RikkaBotan ship as raw SBV2 .safetensors (model_assets), not AIVMX. Convert with the AIVM Generator (aivm-generator, aivis-project) → produces an .aivmx you install per step 4. (Alternative: run raw SBV2 in an isolated Python 3.11 conda/uv env with torch<2.4 — but that pulls in AGPL code; prefer the AIVMX+engine path for a shippable product.)

=== CAST ASSIGNMENT (distinct-per-adjacent, from verified-clean set) ===
Rie-SENSEI(lead adult female, warm/mature) → JVNV-F2 Neutral/Happy. Narrator(gentle rainy-evening) → RikkaBotan asmr (soft) or JVNV-F1 Neutral. Female classmates (sophie/jenny/mika/jodi/stasi/ruparna/rose/angel/nanako/mira) → spread across JVNV-F1 (× emotion styles), RikkaBotan sweet + cool, and vetted AivisHub ACML female originals (e.g. まお/まい/花音 after provenance check) so no two adjacent share a model. Male classmates (henry/aakash/alex/tom/sam/shin/christian/felix/robert/peter/steve/tom2/shaun/xingyu/francis) → JVNV-M1 + JVNV-M2 (× emotion styles) + fumifumi + vetted AivisHub ACML male originals (morioki/にせ/凛音エル/阿井田茂 after provenance check). Use the 7 emotion styles per JVNV speaker to widen apparent-person count without reusing the same style back-to-back. To truly fill 20+ DISTINCT people you MUST add ~10 hand-vetted AivisHub ACML originals — budget provenance-verification time per model page (reject any referencing a real seiyuu/VTuber/game/anime character).

SELF-HOSTED OFFLINE ENGINE + PITCH-ACCENT DRILL PATH (macOS Apple Silicon).

1) INSTALL — Do NOT pip-install raw Style-Bert-VITS2 on this Mac (Python 3.14 has no torch wheels). Instead use the AivisSpeech Engine, which ships as a self-contained PyInstaller binary (bundles its own Python 3.11 + runtime). Grab the macOS arm64 release from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech-Engine/releases (or install the AivisSpeech.app GUI, which embeds the same engine). Requires macOS 13 Ventura+. Apple Silicon is the actively-supported target.

2) RUN — launch the engine binary; it serves a VOICEVOX-compatible HTTP API at http://127.0.0.1:10101. Verify: `curl http://127.0.0.1:10101/version`.

3) LOAD MODELS — download each .aivmx from its hub page (URL: https://hub.aivis-project.com/aivm-models/{uuid}, or programmatically via the model's download endpoint) and register it: `curl -X POST 'http://127.0.0.1:10101/aivm_models/install' -F 'file=@morioki.aivmx'`. List installed speaker/style IDs via `GET /speakers` — each model exposes a speaker UUID and one style_id per style (morioki=1 style; まお=6, みちのくあいり=7, etc.).

4) STORY LINES (323 fixed lines) — for each line: `POST /audio_query?text=<line>&speaker=<style_id>` -> returns an AudioQuery JSON with accent_phrases; then `POST /synthesis?speaker=<style_id>` with that JSON body -> WAV. Batch this offline, one WAV per line, cache by (style_id, text) hash.

5) PITCH-ACCENT DRILL AUDIO (learner-safe) — the accent DOWNSTEP is editable and this is what matters for 平板/頭高/中高/尾高 drills. In the AudioQuery, each accent_phrase has an integer `accent` field = the mora index of the pitch drop (0 = heiban/no drop). Overwrite it from your Kanjium/OJAD accent data per word, then re-synthesize. CAVEAT confirmed from the engine README: the numeric per-mora `pitch` field is returned as a dummy 0.0 and is NOT settable (`consonant_length`/`vowel_length`/`pitch` unsupported) — so you get correct HIGH/LOW accent SHAPE via the accent index, but not fine Hz tuning. For most drill/imitation lines the accent-index path is sufficient and stays learner-safe. If you ever need true per-mora Hz control, that requires raw litagin02/Style-Bert-VITS2 inference under a separate Python 3.11 pyenv/conda env with torch — keep that as an optional side-path, not the default.

6) LICENSING AT SHIP — ACML 1.0 allows commercial use with credit optional; still add a credits screen listing each model + creator to satisfy good practice and the Oz Chat / リアボVC models' requested-credit strings (e.g. 'AivisSpeech: まお', 'morioki (X:@morioki_5)'). Never use these voices to impersonate/pass-off a real person (ACML 1.0 forbids it). zonoko is CC0 (no obligation). Re-verify each model's license on its hub page at ship time in case a creator changes it.

recipes.lane: Offline pitch-accent path for drill audio (no AWS)
recipes.recipe:
OFFLINE PITCH-ACCENT DRILL AUDIO — concrete pipeline (no AWS, no torch/pip).

=== ENGINE: AivisSpeech Engine on macOS Apple Silicon ===
1. Download AivisSpeech.app from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech releases (Apple Silicon native; ships its own ONNX runtime, so Python 3.14 is irrelevant). Engine binary: ~/Applications/AivisSpeech.app/Contents/Resources/AivisSpeech-Engine/run. Launch it (or the .app) → HTTP API on http://127.0.0.1:10101, Swagger at /docs. Engine license LGPL-3.0 (dynamic runtime, does not taint your app). Models (.aivmx) go in ~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models. DO NOT ship the bundled Anneli default (tainted). Install a clean model (see models[]) instead.

=== KANJIUM NUMBER → ACCENT, THE DIRECT BRIDGE ===
Reuse scripts/build-pitch-accents-sql.mjs's existing converter (self-tested ハ'シ / ハシ' / ハシ). Its AquesTalk-style output IS exactly what AivisSpeech /accent_phrases?is_kana=true consumes. Mapping from a Kanjium accent number N over a reading of M moras:
  - N=1 (atamadaka): apostrophe AFTER mora 1  → 箸 はし → "ハ'シ"  (H L; following particle stays low)
  - N=M (odaka): apostrophe AFTER the final mora → 橋 はし → "ハシ'"  (L H, then the particle FALLS)
  - 1<N<M (nakadaka): apostrophe after mora N
  - N=0 (heiban): NO apostrophe → 端 はし → "ハシ"  (L H H…, particle stays HIGH)
Note: for an isolated drill word (no particle) odaka and heiban are audibly identical; the H/L→particle difference only manifests when a following particle is attached in the same accent phrase — handle that only for full sentence lines, not single-word drills.

=== FORCING 箸 (atamadaka) vs 橋 (odaka) VIA THE HTTP API ===
Two-call flow per line/word:
  A) POST /accent_phrases?speaker=<styleId>&is_kana=true  body: "ハ'シ"  (atamadaka)  → returns AccentPhrase[] with accent=1, moras=[{text:"ハ",consonant:"h",vowel:"a",...,pitch:~5.9},{text:"シ",consonant:"sh",vowel:"i",...,pitch:~5.3}]. For 橋 send "ハシ'" → accent=2 (downstep after final mora). For 端 send "ハシ" → accent=0.
     (Schema: AccentPhrase={moras[], accent:int 1-indexed downstep-mora position, pause_mora, is_interrogative}; Mora={text,consonant,consonant_length,vowel,vowel_length,pitch}; pitch is per-mora log-f0.)
  B) Wrap those accent_phrases into an AudioQuery: call POST /audio_query?text=<reading-in-kana>&speaker=<id> to get a full AudioQuery with default speedScale/pitchScale/intonationScale/prosody, then REPLACE its .accent_phrases with the array from step A (this pins the downstep exactly, overriding the model's g2p guess). POST that AudioQuery to /synthesis?speaker=<id> → WAV bytes.
     (Shortcut: you can also directly patch a single AudioQuery.accent_phrases[i].accent integer = your Kanjium N — same effect as the apostrophe kana — but is_kana kana is safer because it also fixes mora segmentation/rendaku.)
  C) ffmpeg -i out.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 48k out.opus (or your existing Web-Audio-bytes path) → cache in R2 keyed by term×reading×kanjiumN×styleId.

Pure-OpenJTalk alternative (no neural model, fully offline, if you ever drop AivisSpeech): pip install pyopenjtalk (needs a Python ≤3.12 venv — system 3.14 won't build it), then build a User Dictionary / patch the accent so extract_fullcontext emits your Kanjium nucleus, or synthesize via OpenJTalk HTS voice. Lower realism; keep it only as a non-neural fallback.

=== VERIFICATION: does the rendered line actually carry the expected accent? ===
Gate every rendered line before caching:
  1) EXPECTED pattern: pyopenjtalk.g2p(reading, kana=False) + pyopenjtalk_g2p_prosody(reading) gives the '[' (rise) ']' (downstep) '#' (phrase-boundary) symbol string; the mora index of ']' = expected downstep. Cross-check it equals your Kanjium N (they must agree; if Kanjium and OpenJTalk disagree, TRUST Kanjium and flag). Equivalently parse extract_fullcontext()'s /A: field (a1==0 marks the accent-nucleus mora).
  2) ACTUAL pattern: extract f0 from the rendered WAV (pyworld.harvest or librosa.pyin), average f0 per mora using the AudioQuery mora boundaries (vowel_length/consonant_length give the timing), and locate the mora after which f0 drops >~15%. That measured downstep-mora must equal the expected one.
  3) SCORE: run PASQA (github.com/lycorp-jp/PASQA, LY Corp's open pitch-accent quality scorer) on the WAV for a per-line accent-correctness score; auto-pass above threshold, queue below-threshold lines for a re-synth with a stronger apostrophe/accent override or manual mora-pitch edit. Minimal-pair regression set to always assert: 箸/橋/端 (はし 1/2/0), 雨/飴 (あめ 1/0), 神/紙 (かみ). Only hand-fix flagged words; never trust neural g2p for anything a learner imitates.

OFFLINE ENGINE + PITCH-ACCENT PIPELINE (macOS Apple Silicon, no AWS/Polly, no pip torch — sidesteps Python 3.14).

1) INSTALL ENGINE (self-contained runtime, no Python env needed): Download the AivisSpeech Engine macOS arm64 build from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech-Engine/releases (or install the AivisSpeech.app desktop bundle, which embeds the same engine). It ships ONNX Runtime + its own interpreter — you do NOT pip-install style-bert-vits2/torch, so the machine's Python 3.14 is irrelevant. Run: ./run  (or launch AivisSpeech.app). It serves an HTTP API on http://127.0.0.1:10101 (override with --port). This is the strongly-preferred path over raw pip SBV2JE.

2) INSTALL VOICE MODELS: For each chosen model, download its .aivmx (ONNX) file — model page hub.aivis-project.com/aivm-models/<uuid>, download endpoint GET https://api.aivis-project.com/v1/aivm-models/<uuid>/download?model_type=AIVMX — and drop it into  ~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models/ . The engine auto-discovers .aivmx at startup. (AivisSpeech.app also has an in-app "install from AivisHub" button and the engine exposes POST /aivm_models/install for scripted install by uuid.) Restart engine; confirm via GET /speakers (returns each model's style IDs).

3) SYNTHESIZE A STORY LINE (2-step VOICEVOX-compatible flow): 
   a. POST /audio_query?speaker=<styleId>&text=<line>  -> returns an AudioQuery JSON whose accent_phrases[].moras[] carry per-mora pitch (accent position). 
   b. POST /synthesis?speaker=<styleId>  with that JSON body -> 24kHz WAV.
   Assign one DISTINCT styleId per character (map the 16 male + 1 neutral models to henry/aakash/alex/tom/sam/shin/christian/felix/robert/peter/steve/tom2/shaun/xingyu/francis + narrator; keep adjacent classmates on different models so no two sound alike). Batch all 323 lines through this loop; cache WAVs by (styleId,textHash).

4) LEARNER-SAFE DRILL / IMITATION LINES: for drill audio, first call /audio_query, then programmatically OVERWRITE moras[].pitch to the canonical Kanjium/OJAD accent for the target word before /synthesis, so the pitch contour is pedagogically correct rather than whatever the model improvised. This per-mora override is the reason to stay on SBV2JE/AivisSpeech rather than a black-box TTS. (You already have the Kanjium D1 pitch data in the yomu-audio worker — reuse it here for the offline path.)

5) LICENSING AT SHIP TIME: ACML 1.0 models (15 of 17) need NO credit and permit the shipped commercial product; just never present the audio as a real person's real voice (impersonation/deepfake is the only ACML bar). For 蒼月ハヤテ (Custom) and M1/M2 (CC BY-SA 4.0) add a credit line in an About/credits screen ("音声モデル: 蒼月ハヤテ" / "jvnv corpus, CC BY-SA 4.0"); CC BY-SA also wants the model file itself, if you redistribute it, kept under CC BY-SA — fine as long as you distribute generated WAVs, not the .aivmx.

NOTE ON RAW SBV2JE: only fall back to pip-installing style-bert-vits2 if you need training/fine-tuning; it requires torch and Python <=3.12, which this Mac cannot satisfy on 3.14 — so use a pyenv/conda 3.11 env in that case. For pure inference of these pre-made models, the bundled AivisSpeech Engine is the correct and only-needed runtime.

recipes.lane: AivisSpeech Engine headless setup + VOICEVOX-compatible batch synthesis on macOS Apple Silicon, feeding pre-made SBV2 JP-Extra voices from AivisHub.
recipes.recipe:
=== A. INSTALL THE ENGINE (macOS arm64, no pip, Python 3.14 irrelevant) ===
1. Download AivisSpeech.app (or the standalone AivisSpeech-Engine) from github.com/Aivis-Project/AivisSpeech/releases (Apple Silicon build). The .app bundles the engine + its own runtime.
2. First run auto-downloads a BERT model (~650MB) + default voice (~250MB) into ~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/. Do NOT pip install style-bert-vits2/torch — the bundled onnxruntime runtime is self-contained, so host Python 3.14 never touches it.

=== B. RUN HEADLESS (HTTP API on :10101) ===
  "/Applications/AivisSpeech.app/Contents/Resources/AivisSpeech-Engine/run" --host 127.0.0.1 --port 10101
Health check + interactive docs: open http://127.0.0.1:10101/docs (Swagger). Engine license: LGPL-3.0. macOS is CPU-only (omit --use_gpu; it is a no-op here). 323 lines = a few minutes one-time.

=== C. INSTALL VOICE MODELS FROM AIVISHUB BY UUID (scriptable) ===
  # download URL format: https://api.aivis-project.com/v1/aivm-models/{UUID}/download?model_type=AIVMX
  install(){ curl --fail -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:10101/aivm_models/install" \
      -F "url=https://api.aivis-project.com/v1/aivm-models/$1/download?model_type=AIVMX"; }
  install a59cb814-0083-4369-8542-f51a29e72af7   # まお (lead-teacher candidate)
  install 47e53151-a378-46f3-abee-ce13aa07feb1   # 阿井田茂 (adult male)
  # ...repeat for each cast UUID in the models[] array.
  # (Manual alt: drop the .aivmx files into ~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models and restart.)
  # List installed + discover each style's global speaker id:
  curl -s http://127.0.0.1:10101/speakers | jq '.[] | {name, styles:[.styles[]|{name,id}]}'
  # Note: the API's per-style local_id (0,1,2..) is NOT the synthesis id — always read the global "id" from /speakers.

=== D. SYNTHESIZE ONE LINE -> WAV (audio_query -> synthesis) ===
  SID=888753760   # a global style id from /speakers (per character/emotion)
  curl -s -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:10101/audio_query?speaker=$SID" \
       --get --data-urlencode "text=おはようございます、今日の授業を始めましょう。" > q.json
  curl -s -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d @q.json \
       -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:10101/synthesis?speaker=$SID" > line.wav
  # Per-call knobs live INSIDE q.json (edit before synthesis): speedScale, pitchScale,
  # intonationScale, volumeScale, prePhonemeLength, postPhonemeLength. Switching character = switch $SID.

=== E. LEARNER-SAFE PITCH-ACCENT DRILL PATH (why SBV2 JP-Extra matters) ===
  q.json.accent_phrases[] carries { moras:[{text,consonant,vowel,pitch}], accent:N }.
  For drill/imitation lines, overwrite accent (the downstep mora index, 1-based) and/or per-mora pitch to the
  textbook Tokyo-dialect accent, then POST the edited query to /synthesis. This guarantees the reference audio
  matches the accent you teach — the reason to self-host SBV2 rather than a black-box TTS. (Optional: POST the
  raw text to /accent_phrases first to get a clean starting frame, or use /mora_pitch helpers if present.)

=== F. ENCODE OPUS (ffmpeg libopus) ===
  ffmpeg -y -i line.wav -c:a libopus -b:a 48k -vbr on -application voip line.opus
  # story narration: -application audio -b:a 64k. Batch: loop lines.tsv (id\ttext\tspeaker_id) -> wav -> opus.

=== G. CASTING STRATEGY (20+ distinct people from the models[] set) ===
Assign one model per character by voice_timbre so no two adjacent voices collide; use each model's built-in
emotional styles (normal/calm/anger/happy/sad/teasing/wistful) for range instead of pitch-shifting one voice.
Where you have more characters than models, reuse a model on a DIFFERENT style + a small pitchScale offset
(<=0.05) and keep it away from its twin in seating order. Suggested anchors: rie(SENSEI, mature lead)->まい妖艶
or まお/おちつき; narrator->hinakoyuhara(MiddleAgedMale, calm) or 阿井田茂/Calm; elders/professor roles->
TANAKA(ElderlyMale) & ろてじん(長老) & 猩々博士; youthful males(henry/alex/felix/sam...)->yukyu, Lux, kokuren,
morioki, fumifumi, 結亜ナル(CC0); youthful females(sophie/jenny/mika/rose/nanako/mira...)->コハク, 花音, るな,
桜音, ほのか, 凛音エル, みちのくあいり; spread ElderlyMale/MiddleAgedMale/Youthful across the cast for age variety.

=== H. ALTERNATIVE (if you prefer managed) ===
Aivis Cloud API (api.aivis-project.com) offers the same models server-side — but the self-hosted engine keeps
the offline drill path and avoids per-call cost; recommended for a shipped product.

recipes.lane: Offline render→QA→R2 pipeline for the 323 fixed academy voice lines
recipes.recipe:
PIPELINE: offline render → accent-QA → Opus → R2, re-runnable/incremental. Files under scripts/academy-voice/.

0) PREREQS (macOS Apple Silicon, one-time)
- Install AivisSpeech.app (bundles its own runtime — avoids this Mac's Python 3.14/torch wall). Start the engine headless: `~/Applications/AivisSpeech.app/Contents/Resources/AivisSpeech-Engine/run --host 127.0.0.1 --port 10101` (or launch the app). Health: `curl localhost:10101/version`.
- Drop chosen AIVMX models into `~/Library/Application Support/AivisSpeech-Engine/Models/` (or POST the AivisHub install endpoint), then `GET /speakers` to read each model's styles and their numeric `style_id`. These style_ids are what /audio_query&/synthesis take as `speaker=`.
- `brew install ffmpeg jq`; `wrangler --version` (auth'd to the account owning the audio R2 bucket).

1) CONFIG: scripts/academy-voice/voice-map.json  — speaker(id) → { aivm_uuid, style_id, style_name, speedScale, pitchScale, intonationScale, model_version }.
   - Assign a DISTINCT base model per adjacent character (not one model + pitch shifts). Seed from the verified-clean set: narrator/rie → RikkaBotan sweet/cool; male cast (henry/aakash/alex/tom/…) → JVNV M1/M2 across its 6 emotions + AivisHub male community models; female cast → amitaro/Koharune Ami + RikkaBotan variants + distinct AivisHub female models. Differentiate further with per-speaker speedScale/pitchScale/intonationScale/style so a dozen base models cover 20+ people.
   - `model_version` is a hand-bumped string per speaker; it is what forces re-render when you change a voice (see step 7 — the sha does NOT change when the model changes, because it hashes only text+speaker).

2) LOAD WORK LIST: read public/academy/audio/voice-lines.json → list of {sha:<manifestKey>, speaker, text}. The manifest key IS the R2 <sha>; use it verbatim so it lines up with whatever the worker looks up. Add a self-check: recompute the hash with the worker's exact algorithm (hash(speaker + '\0' + text) truncated to 12 bytes/24 hex — confirm against worker source) and assert it equals the manifest key; abort on drift so the renderer can never write to a key the worker won't read.
   - Determine the accent-QA target set: lines the learner imitates (non-narrator character drill lines, plus any line tagged as a pitch drill in the academy content). Narrator lines skip the strict accent gate (they still get a sanity pass).

3) INCREMENTAL SKIP (re-runnable): keep scripts/academy-voice/ledger.json { sha: {speaker, model_version, done:true} }. For each line: skip if ledger has it done AND ledger.model_version == voice-map[speaker].model_version. Optionally reconcile once at start with `wrangler r2 object list --prefix voice/` so a fresh checkout re-hydrates the ledger from what's already in R2 instead of re-rendering everything.

4) RENDER (per line): 
   a. `curl -s -X POST "localhost:10101/audio_query?speaker=<style_id>" --get --data-urlencode text="<text>"` → query.json.
   b. Apply per-speaker prosody from voice-map: set query.speedScale / pitchScale / intonationScale / prePhonemeLength / postPhonemeLength.
   c. `curl -s -X POST "localhost:10101/synthesis?speaker=<style_id>" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d @query.json --output line.wav` (24kHz WAV).

5) ACCENT-QA GATE (drill/imitation lines only) — keeps learners safe:
   - Intended pitch pattern comes from the app's existing pitch data (Kanjium/NHK: accent-nucleus / mora count) for the drilled headword(s).
   - Symbolic check: in query.json, for the accent_phrase containing the target word, assert `accent_phrases[].accent` (the downstep mora index) == the expected accent type. If it differs, PATCH accent (and mora boundaries) to the correct value and re-POST /synthesis with the corrected query — this is the whole reason to use AivisSpeech: the mora pitch is editable pre-synthesis.
   - Acoustic confirm: run line.wav through a pitch tracker (librosa.pyin or WORLD f0) and verify the H→L downstep lands on the expected mora within tolerance (and that unvoiced morae aren't spuriously voiced). 
   - On fail after one patch attempt: DO NOT ship the take — log {sha, speaker, word, expected, got} to qa-fails.json and fall back to a known-good "flat/neutral" reference voice for that line so a wrong accent is never taught. Passing takes proceed.

6) ENCODE Opus: `ffmpeg -y -i line.wav -ac 1 -c:a libopus -b:a 32k -vbr on -application voip -ar 48000 line.opus` (mono speech; 24–32 kbps is transparent for narration; bump narrator to -b:a 48k -application audio if you want richer storyteller tone). 

7) R2 PUT keyed like the worker cache: 
   `wrangler r2 object put <BUCKET>/voice/<speaker>/<sha>.opus --file line.opus --content-type "audio/ogg" --cache-control "public, max-age=31536000, immutable"`.
   - Stamp custom metadata so voice-model changes are detectable despite the content-only sha: wrangler supports custom metadata — write `model-version=<voice-map model_version>` (and model uuid/style). On the next run, step 3 compares this against the current map and re-renders+overwrites when a speaker's voice was reassigned. (If a given wrangler build lacks custom-metadata flags, keep model_version authoritative in ledger.json and treat a map bump as "delete the key + re-put".)
   - Mark ledger[sha] = {speaker, model_version, done:true} only after a successful put.

8) VERIFY: for a sample of shas, `curl -I https://audio.yomureader.com/voice/line?text=<enc>&speaker=<id>` and assert 200 + audio/ogg + the object length matches; spot-listen the accent-QA fallback lines.

RE-RUNNABILITY SUMMARY: idempotent by (sha, model_version) via ledger.json + R2 custom metadata; a second run with no map changes does zero engine calls and zero puts; changing one speaker's model_version re-renders only that speaker's lines; the manifest is the single source of truth for the work list and the R2 key. Wrap steps 4–7 in a small Node or Python driver over the manifest with a concurrency cap (2–4 parallel synths; the engine is CPU/ANE-bound) and retry/backoff on 5xx from the engine and from wrangler.
